judges.20.p1.b1.text: Then all the Israelites from Dan to Beersheba and from the land of Gilead came out, and the congregation assembled as one man before the LORD at Mizpah.

judges.20.p1.b2.text: The leaders of all the people and all the tribes of Israel presented themselves in the assembly of God’s people: 400,000 men on foot, armed with swords.

judges.20.p1.b3.text: (Meanwhile the Benjamites heard that the Israelites had gone up to Mizpah.)

judges.20.p1.b4.text: Tell us, how did this wicked thing happen?

judges.20.p2.b1.text: I and my concubine came to Gibeah in Benjamin to spend the night.

judges.20.p2.b2.text: And during the night, the men of Gibeah rose up against me and surrounded the house. They intended to kill me, …

judges.20.p2.b3.text: … because they had committed a lewd and disgraceful act in Israel.

judges.20.p2.b4.text: Behold, all you Israelites, give your advice and verdict here and now.

judges.20.p3.b1.text: Not one of us will return to his tent or to his house.

judges.20.p3.b2.text: Now this is what we will do to Gibeah: We will go against it as the lot dictates.

judges.20.p3.b3.text: We will take ten men out of every hundred from all the tribes of Israel, … to supply provisions for the army

judges.20.p3.b4.text: So all the men of Israel gathered as one man, united against the city.

judges.20.p4.b1.text: What is this wickedness that has occurred among you? … Hand over the wicked men of Gibeah so we can put them to death …

judges.20.p4.b2.text: But the Benjamites refused to heed the voice of their fellow Israelites.

judges.20.p4.b3.text: And from their cities they came together at Gibeah to go out and fight against the Israelites.

judges.20.p4.b4.text: Among all these soldiers there were 700 select left-handers, each of whom could sling a stone at a hair without missing.

judges.20.p5.b1.text: Who of us shall go up first to fight against the Benjamites?

judges.20.p5.b3.text: The next morning the Israelites set out and camped near Gibeah.

judges.20.p5.b4.text: And the Benjamites came out of Gibeah and cut down 22,000 Israelites on the battlefield that day.

judges.20.p6.b1.text: But the Israelite army took courage and again took their battle positions in the same place where they had arrayed themselves on the first day.

judges.20.p6.b2.text: Should we again draw near for battle against our brothers the Benjamites?

judges.20.p6.b4.text: That same day the Benjamites came out against them from Gibeah and cut down another 18,000 Israelites, all of them armed with swords.

judges.20.p7.b1.text: Then the Israelites, all the people, went up to Bethel, where they sat weeping before the LORD. That day they fasted until evening

judges.20.p7.b2.text: (In those days the ark of the covenant of God was there, and Phinehas son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, served before it.)

judges.20.p7.b3.text: Should we again go out to battle against our brothers the Benjamites, or should we stop?

judges.20.p7.b4.text: Fight, for tomorrow I will deliver them into your hand.

judges.20.p8.b1.text: So Israel set up an ambush around Gibeah.

judges.20.p8.b2.text: On the third day the Israelites went up against the Benjamites and arrayed themselves against Gibeah as they had done before.

judges.20.p8.b3.text: We are defeating them as before,

judges.20.p8.b4.text: Let us retreat and draw them away from the city onto the roads.

judges.20.p9.b1.text: So all the men of Israel got up from their places and arrayed themselves at Baal-tamar, and the Israelites in ambush charged from their positions west of Gibeah.

judges.20.p9.b2.text: Then 10,000 select men from all Israel made a frontal assault against Gibeah, and the battle was fierce.

judges.20.p9.b3.text: But the Benjamites did not realize that disaster was upon them.

judges.20.p9.b4.text: The LORD defeated Benjamin in the presence of Israel, … Then the Benjamites realized they had been defeated.

judges.20.p10.b1.text: The men in ambush rushed suddenly against Gibeah; … The men of Israel had arranged a signal with the men in ambush: When they sent up a great cloud of smoke from the city,

judges.20.p10.b2.text: They are defeated before us as in the first battle.

judges.20.p10.b3.text: But when the column of smoke began to go up from the city, the Benjamites looked behind them and saw the whole city going up in smoke.

judges.20.p10.b4.text: Then the men of Israel turned back on them, and the men of Benjamin were terrified when they realized that disaster had come upon them.

judges.20.p11.b1.text: So they fled before the men of Israel toward the wilderness, but the battle overtook them, and the men coming out of the cities struck them down there.

judges.20.p11.b2.text: And 18,000 Benjamites fell, all men of valor.

judges.20.p11.b3.text: Then the Benjamites turned and fled toward the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon, and Israel cut down 5,000 men on the roads. …

judges.20.p12.b1.text: That day 25,000 Benjamite swordsmen fell, all men of valor.

judges.20.p12.b2.text: But 600 men turned and fled into the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon, where they stayed four months.

judges.20.p12.b3.text: And the men of Israel turned back against the other Benjamites … And they burned down all the cities in their path.
